tier_reason: benchmarks/results-avr.ods is a bare first-party table (no headers, no toolchain or simulator versions, no commit link) whose rows match the record exactly (fix16_add 64/67/71 vs float add 93/135/183, fix16_sub 71/75/83 vs 94/135/189, fix16_mul 226/377/476 vs 81/140/148, fix16_div 132/637/1272 vs 80/450/499); compiler, flags and the simulated ATmega128 have to be inferred from benchmarks/Makefile and benchmarks/benchmark.c, avr-gcc and simulavr versions are unstated, and the harness itself mis-times two of its six float rows, so it stays C rather than A.

corrections.caveats: Mixed result from the project's own spreadsheet: fixed point wins only add and subtract (about 2x) and loses multiply (2.7x slower) and divide (1.4x slower) to avr-libc/libgcc software float on this 8-bit target; only the add/sub rows support a 'faster' claim. The spreadsheet has no column headers (its embedded chart labels the columns only 'Sloupec C/D/E', Czech for 'Column C/D/E'); min/avg/max is inferred from benchmarks/interface.c print(), which the AVR build links. It states no avr-gcc, avr-libc or simulavr version. The timing harness has no compiler barriers: the float sqrtf and expf rows (8 cycles min/avg/max) show avr-gcc moved those libm calls out of the timed region, so no sqrt or exp comparison is valid; the add/sub/mul/div float rows (80-499 cycles) look like real soft-float calls. fix16_add/fix16_sub are timed as out-of-line calls with overflow checking (FIXMATH_NO_OVERFLOW unset); with that option they become static inline plain integer adds. The file was added by contributor maruncz in PR #33 (commit 0c88e55, merged 2021-05-03, ods metadata 2021-05-01), the same PR that fixed fix16_div failing unit tests under GCC >= 9 and an overflow corner case; whether the div row was measured before or after that fix is not stated, and fix16.c changed again on 2023-08-08 (FIXMATH_NO_HARD_DIVISION refactor), so the numbers may not match current code. The Makefile also has a Cortex-M3 QEMU target, but no ARM results are committed. A Wikipedia statement that libfixmath atan2 takes 26.3% of float time on a Cortex-M0 was seen only as a WebSearch snippet (en.wikipedia.org EGRESS_BLOCKED) with no benchmark code or source in the repo; unverified. Fixed point is compared only with float, not with another fixed-point library. The README FIXMATH_FAST_SIN '159% the speed' figure is a self-comparison. README says 'Not actively maintained, pull requests welcome' although commits landed 2026-02-04 and 2026-07-13 (fix16_asin/atan2 boundary cases, fix16_to_int overflow).

notes: Numbers in claimed_speedup match benchmarks/results-avr.ods exactly and the derived ratios are correct; metadata (MIT, 886 stars, 191 forks, last commit 2026-07-13, not a fork, not archived) checks out. Shortcomings to record: only add/sub are faster (mul 2.7x and div 1.4x slower than soft float), sqrtf/expf rows are harness artifacts (calls hoisted out of the timed region), no toolchain versions, numbers from a 2021 contributor PR that also fixed fix16_div, Cortex-M0 atan2 26.3% figure snippet only.
